newsitem.title: UK: BT launches yacht tracking Web site.
newsitem.headline: BT launches yacht tracking Web site.

text.p: Yachting fans will next month be able to follow what has been dubbed the world's toughest ocean yacht race on a British Telecommunications World Wide Web site for the BT Global Challenge, the group said on Wednesday.

Computer-literate armchair yachtsmen and women can now get details on all aspects of the 30,000 mile race that starts in Southampton on September 29, ranging from details about teams and vessels to the weather conditions the crews are enduring.

Fourteen, 67-foot steel yachts are sailing against all prevailing winds and currents to four continents stopping at Wellington in New Zealand, Boston in the U.S., Rio de Janeiro in Brazil, Sydney in Australia and Cape Town, South Africa.

"To monitor and communicate the results of the world's toughtest yacht race, BT has combined the power of the latest global satellite communications technology with the reach and flexibility of the Internet," the company said.
Other information available on the Web site includes video and audio clips and the opportunity for race followers to ask participants questions.
Updates on postitions, routes and tactics will be on a six-hourly basis except at the beginning, during direct challenges and at the end of the race. Then they will posted at 10 minute intervals.

Unveiling the site, BT -- which is sponsoring the race partly to get its brand better known worldwide -- told reporters it was hoping to attract several hundreds of thousands of "visitors" to its Web site per day.
"We feel we are global challengers ourselves," said Richard Slogrove, director global marketing. "In the UK we are the incumbent telecom company, but outside, we are a predator."
Web site visitors can also take part in the race, creating their own "virtual" yacht, choosing a crew, food and guiding their vessels through the same conditions of the real teams.
It may be cheaper than the 18,750 stg it is costing the volunteers to take part in the real race, but neglect your yacht and it will sink, the company warned.
The overall winner gets a holiday for two in Cape Town plus 500 stg spending money, a BT spokesman said.
